# glad

OpenGL / WGL function loader, generated by [glad2](https://github.com/Dav1dde/glad).

Used by the OpenGL video backend (`graphics/vid_backend_ogl.cpp`). The DirectX 7
backend does not touch any of this.

## Why glad and not GLEW

The abandoned `upgrade-graphics-system` branch referenced GLEW in every
`.vcxproj` include path and did `#pragma comment(lib, "glew32s.lib")`, but the
library was never committed — that branch cannot build. glad generates plain
`.c`/`.h` that compile straight into the `graphics` project, so there is no
static library to build, vendor, or ship.

## Regenerating

Generated with glad2. To reproduce exactly:

```bash
python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/python -m pip install glad2
python -m glad --api="gl:core=3.3" --extensions="" --out-path=out c --loader
python -m glad --api="wgl=1.0" --extensions="WGL_ARB_create_context,WGL_ARB_create_context_profile,WGL_ARB_pixel_format,WGL_ARB_multisample,WGL_EXT_swap_control" --out-path=out c --loader
```

Then copy `out/include` and `out/src` over this directory.

`--extensions=""` on the GL call is deliberate: without it glad emits all 623
registered extensions, which inflates the header from ~2k lines to ~14k for no
benefit. We target **GL 3.3 core** and nothing outside it.

The WGL extension list is the minimum needed to create a core-profile context:
`create_context` + `create_context_profile` for `wglCreateContextAttribsARB`,
`pixel_format` + `multisample` for `wglChoosePixelFormatARB`, and
`EXT_swap_control` for vsync.

## Files

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `include/glad/gl.h`, `src/gl.c` | GL 3.3 core entry points and `gladLoaderLoadGL` |
| `include/glad/wgl.h`, `src/wgl.c` | WGL entry points and `gladLoaderLoadWGL` |
| `include/KHR/khrplatform.h` | Khronos base types, required by the above |
